title: REMU: Memory-aware Radiation Emulation via Dual Addressing for In-orbit Deep Learning System
problem: COTS GPUs deployed in space face radiation-induced memory errors but lack effective tools to link radiation faults to runtime DNN behavior; existing emulation methods fail to map errors from physical memory to DNN execution.
motivation: Space applications require reliable on-orbit DNN inference; understanding radiation resilience requires bridging the gap between fault injection and actual model degradation.
method: REMU tracks memory addresses through three layers—the abstract addresses programs use, physical chip locations, and actual DRAM storage—so radiation-induced bit flips at the DRAM level map directly to the neural network calculations they corrupt. This dual-addressing mechanism (tracking addresses through multiple memory translation layers) enables efficient error injection: researchers inject simulated radiation faults at the DRAM level and measure how the AI model's predictions fail.
key_novelty: The core contribution is dual-addressing (tracking memory addresses from virtual through physical through DRAM layers) to connect radiation-induced memory faults directly to neural network inference behavior.
contributions: Dual addressing mechanism for virtual-physical-DRAM mapping
Precise radiation error injection to DNN runtime
Evaluation on 10 DNN models and 2 in-orbit computing tasks
Insights into resilience of on-orbit DNN inference to space radiation
